name: AD Module LDAP & Filter Queries (Advanced Enumeration)
description: High-value LDAP and AD Module filter queries for CRTP-style domain enumeration: AS-REP roastable accounts, unconstrained/constrained delegation, PASSWD_NOTREQD, adminCount=1 principals, Protected Users, and OU-scoped searches. These pinpoint the accounts worth attacking without dumping the whole directory.
notes:
=== WHY FILTER QUERIES ===
Instead of dumping every object, target the accounts that lead to compromise:
accounts without pre-auth (AS-REP), delegation-enabled hosts, weak-flag accounts,
and protected/high-value principals.

=== AS-REP ROASTABLE (no pre-auth) ===
  Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth
  # PowerView:  Get-DomainUser -PreauthNotRequired

=== UNCONSTRAINED DELEGATION (computers) ===
  Get-ADComputer -Filter {TrustedForDelegation -eq $true} -Properties TrustedForDelegation
  # PowerView:  Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained

=== CONSTRAINED DELEGATION ===
  Get-ADObject -Filter {msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo -like '*'} -Properties msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo
  # PowerView:  Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth ; Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth

=== PASSWORD NOT REQUIRED (UAC PASSWD_NOTREQD) ===
  Get-ADUser -Filter {UserAccountControl -band 32} -Properties UserAccountControl
  # PowerView:  Get-DomainUser -UACFilter PASSWD_NOTREQD

=== ADMINCOUNT = 1 (protected / historically privileged) ===
  Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(adminCount=1)' -Properties adminCount
  # PowerView:  Get-DomainUser -AdminCount

=== PROTECTED USERS group members ===
  Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'Protected Users'

=== DISABLED ACCOUNTS ===
  Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=2)'

=== KERBEROASTABLE (has SPN) ===
  Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(&(objectClass=user)(servicePrincipalName=*))' -Properties servicePrincipalName

=== OU-SCOPED SEARCH ===
  Get-ADUser -SearchBase 'OU=Servers,DC=<domain>' -Filter *

=== TIP ===
Use -Server <dc_fqdn> to target a specific DC, and pipe to select samaccountname to keep output tight.

recommended.note: General AD Module enumeration; these filters refine it to attack targets.
The TrustedForDelegation filter feeds delegation abuse.

defense.why_it_works: LDAP allows any authenticated user to read most directory attributes, so targeted filters (UAC flags, delegation attributes, SPNs, adminCount) reveal the exact weak or privileged accounts an attacker should pursue.
defense.prerequisites: Any authenticated domain user and LDAP access to a DC.
defense.impact: Precise target selection - the enumeration that precedes AS-REP roasting, Kerberoasting, delegation abuse, and ACL attacks.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.002] Directory Service Access auditing (Event 4662) and, where enabled, verbose LDAP query logging (Event 1644 on the DC) showing repetitive filtered queries for delegation/UAC/SPN attributes from a workstation; unusual volume of AD Module / LDAP reads from a single host.
defense.artifacts: 4662 object-access events on user/computer objects; 1644 LDAP query logs (if enabled); PowerShell 4104 script blocks referencing Get-ADUser/Get-DomainUser filters.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| stats count by Account_Name, Computer
| where count>200

index=wineventlog source="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational" EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*DoesNotRequirePreAuth*" OR ScriptBlockText="*TrustedForDelegation*"
| table _time, Computer, UserID, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4662
| summarize count() by Account, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where count_ > 200
| sort by count_ desc
defense.prevention: You cannot block authenticated LDAP reads, so focus on detection and reducing attack surface: eliminate no-preauth and PASSWD_NOTREQD accounts, remove unnecessary delegation, empty adminCount residue, and deploy Microsoft Defender for Identity (flags reconnaissance). Enable LDAP query logging on DCs for high-value monitoring.
defense.evasion: Query a single attribute at a time and pace requests to stay under volume thresholds; use the AD Module (signed Microsoft binary) rather than noisier tools.
defense.misconfiguration: Accounts left with no pre-auth, PASSWD_NOTREQD, or unnecessary delegation; stale adminCount=1 residue - all trivially discoverable by filter.
defense.secure_config:
# Remediate the accounts the filters expose:
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} | Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false
# Remove unneeded delegation; audit adminCount=1 residue; enforce strong service-account passwords.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Kerberoastable users (has SPN)
variations.description: Finds all AD user accounts with a Service Principal Name (SPN) set - these accounts are vulnerable to Kerberoasting, where their service ticket can be requested and cracked offline to recover the password.

variations.label: Protected Users group members
variations.description: Queries Active Directory group objects to enumerate group memberships and identify privilege relationships.

variations.label: Disabled accounts (LDAP bitwise)
variations.description: Queries Active Directory user objects with specific filters to identify accounts of interest for further enumeration or attack.

variations.label: OU-scoped user search
variations.description: Searches for user accounts within a specific Organizational Unit (OU). Scoping enumeration to an OU helps focus on a particular department or admin boundary rather than enumerating the entire domain.

variations.label: PowerView equivalents
variations.description: Uses PowerView to find accounts with Kerberos pre-auth disabled. These are AS-REP Roastable - you can request and crack their authentication data without needing any credentials.

explain:
A set of LDAP / AD-module filter queries that pinpoint attack targets without noisy full dumps. The lead example finds AS-REP roastable accounts:
  Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true}   accounts with pre-auth disabled
  -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth   include that attribute in the output
Other queries in the set cover Kerberoastable (servicePrincipalName=*), disabled accounts (userAccountControl bitwise), adminCount=1, Protected Users, and OU-scoped searches - each returns just the principals worth attacking.
